item.title: China's Huawei convicted in sprawling US criminal trial over Iran business
item.description:
By Karen Freifeld

NEW YORK, Nov 24 (Reuters) - Chinese telecommunications equipment maker Huawei was convicted by a jury in New York City on Tuesday in a sprawling US criminal case on charges that it deceived banks about its business in Iran and stole trade secrets from American companies.

The verdict came in a criminal case that began in 2018, with the US government the following year placing Huawei on a trade blacklist that restricted its access to US technology amid American concerns that Huawei posed national security risks.

item.title: Israel's Eisenkot clinches first coalition agreement in bid to form government
item.description:
By Steven Scheer

JERUSALEM, Nov 24 (Reuters) - Israel'sYashar party, led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, said on Tuesday it agreed to sign a coalition pact with a right-wing opposition party as it seeks to form a government following last month's election.

Yashar said that Eisenkot had met with Avigdor Lieberman, head of the Israel Our Home party, earlier on Tuesday and they agreed on a deal afterward, the first such alliance since the election.

item.title: Senior member of Turkish ruling party resigns amid fund probe
item.description:
ANKARA, Nov 24 (Reuters) - Hayati Yazici, a senior member and founder of Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan's ruling AK Party, said on Tuesday he was resigning from the party's leadership as a probe into alleged market manipulation and insider trading widened to include his son.

Since September, Turkish investment funds that had concentrated their holdings in thinly traded stocks have been unable to meet investor withdrawals, prompting regulators to liquidate 131 funds and launch a criminal probe that has involved several senior officials and members of government.

item.title: Houthis won't seize Aden, Yemeni government forces say
item.description:
By Phil Stewart and Timour Azhari

WASHINGTON/RIYADH, Nov 24 (Reuters) - Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis have pushed as close as 60 km (37 miles) to Aden, the temporary capital of the country's internationally recognised government, but they will not capture the city, Yemen's military said on Tuesday.

"I'll speak to you frankly. The situation is not where we want it to be. But it's not as dire as reported," Colonel Majed Abdullah Al-Nuzaily, spokesperson for Yemen's armed forces, told a group of reporters via video link.

item.title: Explainer-What are the disputes between Iraq's federal government and Kurdistan region?
item.description:
Nov 24 (Reuters) - Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi on Tuesday ordered federal authorities to take over border crossings in the semi-autonomous Kurdistan region and directed the oil ministry to manage oilfields under Kurdish security control in four provinces, following an oil smuggling investigation at the state-run North Oil Company.

The orders are part of a broader crackdown byZaidi against oil smuggling. They also reopen long-running disputes between Baghdad and the Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG) overcontrol of oil, money, territory and trade.

item.title: Protests in Jerusalem after Palestinian student activist's arrest
item.description:
Dozens of students and professors protested outside a Jerusalem court on Tuesday where a Palestinian student activist was tried for undisclosed charges after being arrested at his university last week, an AFP journalist reported.

Mahdi Tunsi, 26, is a student from Israeli-annexed east Jerusalem who was arrested by Israeli police at his dormitory in early November, the Hebrew University said in a statement, adding that it was notified of the arrest minutes before it took place.
